```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

DATA = Path("data/outcomes/italy-almalaurea/outcomes.csv")
df = pd.read_csv(DATA)
one = df[df["years_after_phd"] == 1].set_index("indicator")
three = df[df["years_after_phd"] == 3].set_index("indicator")

def cell(frame, key):
    row = frame.loc[key]
    val = row["value"]
    if pd.isna(val):
        return "not published"
    unit = row["unit"]
    if unit == "percent":
        return f"{val:.1f}%"
    if unit == "euro":
        return f"€{val:,.0f}"
    if unit == "count":
        return f"{val:,.0f}"
    if unit == "months":
        return f"{val:.1f} months"
    if unit == "score":
        return f"{val:.1f} / 10"
    if unit == "hours":
        return f"{val:.1f}"
    if unit == "years":
        return f"{val:.1f}"
    return str(val)
```

These figures are **not mathematics PhDs**. AlmaLaurea’s closest official area is **scienze di base** (basic sciences). That grouping includes mathematics and also physics, chemistry, computer science, earth sciences, and related programmes.

The 1-year table is PhDs of 2024, interviewed in 2025. The 3-year table is PhDs of 2022 at a **smaller set of universities**. They are not the same people followed over time.

Source: AlmaLaurea databank, survey year 2025, area `scienze di base`, retrieved 15 August 2026. [SOURCES.md](data/outcomes/italy-almalaurea/SOURCES.md).

The full cell list is [outcomes.csv](data/outcomes/italy-almalaurea/outcomes.csv). How it was copied is in [EXTRACT.md](data/outcomes/italy-almalaurea/EXTRACT.md).

```{python}
istat = pd.read_csv("data/outcomes/italy-istat/outcomes.csv")

def icell(field, key):
    row = istat[(istat["field"] == field) & (istat["indicator"] == key)]
    if row.empty:
        return "not published"
    val = row["value"].iloc[0]
    unit = row["unit"].iloc[0]
    if pd.isna(val):
        return "not published"
    if unit == "percent":
        return f"{val:.1f}%"
    if unit == "count":
        return f"{val:,.0f}"
    if unit == "months":
        return f"{val:.1f} months"
    return str(val)
```

# ISTAT 2025 — four and six years out

This is a **different field** from the AlmaLaurea tables above. Do not read the two blocks as a time series.

ISTAT’s closest official group is **Scientifico**. The report’s footnote: biology, chemistry, biotechnology, nutrition science, **mathematics, statistics**, and physics.

Interview year 2025. Cohorts: 2019 (six years after the degree) and 2021 (four years). Population `{python} icell("all", "population_total")` PhDs; `{python} icell("all", "interviewed")` interviews (response rate `{python} icell("all", "response_rate")`).

Source: [SOURCES.md](data/outcomes/italy-istat/SOURCES.md).

## Scientifico group

| | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Share of all Italian PhDs in these two cohorts | `{python} icell("Scientifico", "share_of_phds")` |
| Employment rate (4–6 years) | `{python} icell("Scientifico", "employment_rate")` |
| Men | `{python} icell("Scientifico", "employment_rate_men")` |
| Women | `{python} icell("Scientifico", "employment_rate_women")` |
| Scholarship for at least part of the doctorate | `{python} icell("Scientifico", "scholarship_during_phd")` |
| Training period abroad during the doctorate | `{python} icell("Scientifico", "trained_abroad")` |

ISTAT does **not** print occupation, pay, or school teaching for Scientifico alone.

## All Italian PhDs — including school

These sector shares are **all fields**, not Scientifico.

| Among the employed (2025) | Share |
| --- | ---: |
| University education | `{python} icell("all", "sector_university")` |
| Non-university education (schools and other) | `{python} icell("all", "sector_non_university_education")` |
| Public research institutes | `{python} icell("all", "sector_public_research")` |
| Private research institutes | `{python} icell("all", "sector_private_research")` |
| Industry | `{python} icell("all", "sector_industry")` |

*Istruzione non universitaria* is the first official school-sector cell we have. It is still **not** a high-school mathematics-teacher count.

Among all PhDs in that sector (Tavola 6):

| | Share |
| --- | ---: |
| Little or not at all satisfied with pay | `{python} icell("all", "school_dissatisfied_pay")` |
| Little or not at all satisfied with career prospects | `{python} icell("all", "school_dissatisfied_career")` |
| Little or not at all satisfied with use of doctoral knowledge | `{python} icell("all", "school_low_use_of_phd")` |

The report also states that 85.3% of doctorate holders who work *nella scuola* have net monthly pay under €2,000. That sentence is not a mathematics-only figure.

Full cells: [outcomes.csv](data/outcomes/italy-istat/outcomes.csv).
